subject: Coffee & Tea
title: What Happens During Roasting
description: Learn What Happens During Roasting in one minute.

hook.text: Green coffee beans have no coffee flavor. Roasting triggers over 1,000 chemical reactions that create it.

buildup.text: Beans enter the roaster at 200°C. Moisture evaporates, then sugars and amino acids start reacting.

discovery.text: The Maillard reaction—same as searing a steak—creates hundreds of flavor and aroma compounds.

twist.text: Caramelization happens separately, breaking sugars into sweet, nutty, and bitter molecules all at once.

climax.text: A roaster's job is controlling time and temperature to balance these reactions for the desired flavor.

punchline.text: Green, tasteless seeds become complex flavor bombs. Heat does it all.

quiz.question: What reaction is primarily responsible for coffee's roasted flavors?
